tagline: Run the platform the business lives in — identity, email, Teams, files, and the policies that keep them safe.
what_you_do: You administer the Microsoft 365 tenant a company works inside all day: creating and offboarding users in Entra ID, assigning licenses, keeping Exchange Online mail flowing, managing Teams and SharePoint/OneDrive sharing, enrolling laptops and phones through Intune, and rolling out the security and compliance policies that hold it all together. It's a huge, real slice of the job market that career sites mostly ignore. It's usually a second rung, not a first job — most people reach it from the help desk, where M365 tickets are already half the queue.
day_in_life: Work the morning queue — a locked-out account, a license request, a 'my email is missing' ticket
Trace a mail-flow problem through Exchange Online message trace to a misfiring transport rule
Stand up a Team and SharePoint site for a new project, with sharing settings that won't leak data
Pilot a conditional access policy on a test group before it touches the whole company
Read the Microsoft 365 message center and flag which of this month's changes will break someone's workflow

salary.entry: ~$55,000–$75,000 to start (industry figure for junior M365/collaboration admin roles)
salary.growth: Steady — nearly every business runs on M365 and someone has to administer it
salary.note: U.S. BLS figure for Network and Computer Systems Administrators (15-1244) — the closest BLS proxy, since there's no dedicated M365 admin code. A median is the midpoint of everyone employed, so entry pay runs lower, and the entry range here is an industry estimate, not BLS. Verify against the live BLS page before deciding.

downsides: The work is ticket-driven, so your day gets interrupted constantly. Microsoft moves the cheese relentlessly — admin centers reorganize, licenses get renamed, features shift between plans — and you re-learn the map every year. Change windows are political: everyone wants improvements, nobody wants downtime. And when email breaks, you get blamed whether or not it was your change. It's also rarely a first job — plan to earn it from the help desk.

fits_if: You like being the person who knows how the whole platform fits together
You're patient with end users and good at translating tech into plain language
You enjoy steady operational improvement more than greenfield building
less_ideal_if: You want deep engineering work over broad administration
Constant interruptions and ticket queues drain you
You'd rather not live inside one vendor's ecosystem

skills.name: Identity fundamentals (Entra ID)
skills.note: Users, groups, licensing, MFA — identity is the spine of everything else in M365.

skills.name: Exchange Online & mail flow
skills.note: Mailboxes, message trace, transport rules — the skill you'll be judged on when email breaks.

skills.name: Security & compliance policies
skills.note: Conditional access, sharing controls, retention — where admin work meets real risk.

skills.name: PowerShell & Microsoft Graph
skills.note: The difference between clicking through portals and administering at scale.

skills.name: Change communication
skills.note: Warning users before you move their cheese is half the job.

certs.title: Microsoft SC-900
certs.reason: Security, compliance, and identity fundamentals — the concepts M365 administration is built on, and the right fundamentals entry now that MS-900 is retired.

certs.title: Microsoft MD-102
certs.reason: Endpoint Administrator — the associate cert proving you can manage devices with Intune, the step up from fundamentals.

certs.title: MS-900 (Retired)
certs.reason: Microsoft retired the old M365 fundamentals exam on March 31, 2026. If it was on your plan, read this before studying toward a dead exam.

cert_note: Honest priority check: a documented tenant you built yourself outweighs any of these on a junior resume — the certs structure the learning and pass filters. Note: MS-900, the old fundamentals exam, was retired in March 2026 (AB-900 is its successor) — SC-900 is the sensible fundamentals start today.

trial.objective: Administer a real Microsoft 365 tenant: create users and groups, assign licenses, and set a sharing policy — the actual daily work, not a simulation.
trial.disclosure: Requires creating a free Microsoft account and a Microsoft 365 Developer/trial tenant. Fully local fallback: map your own household's accounts, sharing, and permissions on paper as an admin design exercise.

roadmap.title: Learn the platform from the admin side
roadmap.focus: Spin up a free Microsoft 365 Developer/trial tenant and work through Microsoft Learn's free M365 admin paths. Break things in your tenant, not someone's business.

roadmap.title: Ground the concepts
roadmap.focus: Earn Microsoft SC-900 — security, compliance, and identity are the ideas every M365 decision hangs on, and it's the cheapest credible signal you can put on a resume.

roadmap.title: Build a documented tenant
roadmap.focus: In your lab tenant: users and groups, licensing, conditional access, a Teams/SharePoint structure with sane sharing, and an Intune-enrolled device. Write it up — that document is your portfolio. MD-102 validates the endpoint half.

roadmap.title: Earn it from the help desk
roadmap.focus: Take every M365 ticket you can, become the escalation person for Exchange and Teams problems, then apply for junior M365/collaboration admin roles inside and outside your company.

adjacent_paths.reason: The same identity-and-endpoint discipline at the infrastructure layer.
